issue_context.title: Possible bug for `LoggerMessageAttribute` generator when having an `ExpressionBody`
issue_context.body:
### Description

I just was reading through the code. I didn't try to reproduce, but the following condition should check for `ExpressionBody` as well:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2330b4bef645bf8bcd3011f35968e55192c697f5/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions/gen/LoggerMessageGenerator.Parser.cs#L276-L280

I think currently it will try to generate a code that later fails to compile instead of giving a neat diagnostic to the user.

### Reproduction Steps

Have a method attributed with `LoggerMessageAttribute` which has an expression body.

### Expected behavior

`LoggingMethodHasBody` diagnostic is produced.

### Actual behavior

Likely it won't be produced (judging by the code). Either way it would be good to add a test.

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

_No response_

### Other information

_No response_

review_comments: Sounds like a very reasonable idea. Just to clarify, the existing method body test does not cover this test case either. Would be good to add for both `Body` and `ExpressionBody` tests?
Yes - I think it would be ideal for both to be tested.

What's the expected behavior for the following code? 
```
[LoggerMessage(EventId = 0, Level = LogLevel.Debug, Message = ""M1"")]
static partial void M1(ILogger logger);

static partial void M1(ILogger logger) { }
```

Currently, this code won't generate any diagnostic because the method with body doesn't have the `LoggerMessageAttribute` applied and all the checks are skipped. Source code is [here](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/9028dc2d715a827a21a5ffbd029bc7a24073406b/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions/gen/LoggerMessageGenerator.Parser.cs#L102). The checks are done within the `foreach`.

If that's an issue, and user does this in their solution, they are likely to get a [CS0756 compile error](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/misc/cs0756) because the partial method `M1` has more than one implementations.

IMHO It's probably a separate and a bigger issue than the OG bug we're trying to fix, and I'm happy to create a separate issue.

> IMHO It's probably a separate and a bigger issue than the OG bug we're trying to fix, and I'm happy to create a separate issue.
